title: Tenant failover prioritization and graceful capacity shedding (Dedicated)
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem statement: Customers on Dedicated pools can experience noisy-neighbor or sudden demand spikes that degrade tail latency for higher-priority tenants and trigger costly over-provisioning. We need a predictable, auditable mechanism to prioritize failover and shed capacity gracefully so high-SLA workloads remain within targets while low-priority traffic is degraded in controlled ways.

Scope: This PRD covers product requirements for: (1) a tenant prioritization model (priority classes + epoch windows) for Dedicated capacity routing and preemption; (2) graceful capacity shedding policies (rate-limit downgrade, forced-sampling, cold-path routing) configurable per-tenant or per-reservation; (3) a borrowing/ledger mechanism to support short-lived capacity loans with automatic reconciliation; (4) admin and tenant-facing controls in Console to set priority, recovery budget, and rollback thresholds; (5) telemetry/dashboarding and per-route acceptance tests.

Out of scope: pricing model changes, long-term contractual changes to reserved commit tiers, and on-prem packaging changes (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: Priority model implemented so operators can assign one of: critical, high, normal, best-effort to any reservation or tenant via Console and API
During simulated 2x traffic spike test, tenants in critical/high priority maintain P95 latency <= 150ms and success rate >= 99% while best-effort traffic is degraded in controlled steps
Capacity-borrowing ledger records loans with start/end timestamps and is reconciled automatically within 10 minutes of recovery window
Console exposes controls: priority class, recovery budget (tokens/min), graceful-shed policy (percent drop, rate-limit), and rollback threshold with explanation and audit log entries

Automated end-to-end acceptance tests (CI) that replay a recorded spike scenario against a staging Dedicated cluster and assert SLA gates pass for priority tenants and that fallback policies trigger for low-priority tenants
Operation runbook and public-facing KB article created describing behaviour, expected customer signals, and recommended tenant config templates
Instrumentation emits events and metrics for preemptions, shed decisions, loan issuance, and per-tenant latency/cost delta with dashboards linked in PRD
outcome_metrics: P95 latency for critical and high priority tenants (target <= 150ms)
SLA success rate for critical tenants (target >= 99%)
Number of emergency preemptions per week (target < 1 per 1,000 tenant-days)
Capacity utilization variance during spikes (target reduce over-provisioning by 15%)
Mean reconciliation time for capacity loans (target <= 10 minutes)
rollout_plan: Alpha: feature gated behind "priority-alloc-alpha" flag; enable for internal tenants and 3 pilot customers (2 weeks)
Beta: open to 10 customers with signed test plan and dedicated staging (4 weeks)
GA: enable via Console for all Dedicated accounts with default policy set to normal; migration script to backfill priority class = normal for existing tenants
Post-GA: monitor metrics for 4 weeks, run iterative tuning to reduce false-preemptions; provide support playbook to SRE and CSM

implementation_constraints: Must work with existing autoscaler and reservation APIs (no DB schema sweeping changes)
Ledger must be append-only and compatible with current audit logging route (minimal runtime overhead)
Preemption decisions should be idempotent and retry-safe across controller restarts
Policy evaluation must complete within 20ms on the request path to avoid adding latency to non-shed-tenants
qa_plan: Unit tests for priority evaluation and loan ledger reconciliation
Integration tests that replay captured production traces with injected spikes
Chaos test: kill a subset of workers during a spike and assert graceful shed behavior
DR test: simulate network partition between controller and agents and validate that audit logs remain consistent
